result.sentence: At 75 MW, this battery runs 5.33 hours; it delivers 360.0 MWh and needs 423.5 MWh to recharge.

work.method: Duration is energy ÷ power; C-rate is power ÷ energy. Depth of discharge limits the energy delivered, and round-trip efficiency is a loss taken on charging, so charging energy is delivered energy ÷ efficiency. The same convention holds in the workbench's battery screen.
steps: Duration at rated power: 400 MWh ÷ 100 MW = 4 h.
Usable delivered energy: 400 MWh × 90% depth of discharge = 360 MWh.
Charging energy: 360 MWh ÷ 85% round-trip efficiency = 423.5 MWh, with the losses taken on charging.
assumptions: Rated energy is the battery's nameplate energy at its rated power; real duration falls at high power and low temperature.
Depth of discharge and round-trip efficiency are the values entered; degradation is not modeled.
